title: Process peak memory
responsibility: Runs a command under the system time utility with a deadline and returns peak resident bytes when the platform report is available, otherwise an unavailable reason.

inputs.name: peakMemory.command
inputs.description: Names the executable that `/usr/bin/time` runs after its platform flag. This input matters only after the `/usr/bin/time` existence check passes.

inputs.name: peakMemory.args
inputs.description: Lists the argument strings appended after the executable and platform-specific time flag. Each array element is passed as one command argument.

inputs.name: peakMemory.input
inputs.description: Provides the text supplied to the timed command's standard input. It may be empty; the wrapper does not otherwise inspect it.

inputs.name: peakMemory.timeoutMs
inputs.description: Sets the bounded runner's timeout in milliseconds for the timed command. Defaults to 60000; this wrapper passes the value through without validating its range.

outputs.name: peakMemory
outputs.description: Resolves to `{bytes}` when `/usr/bin/time` exits successfully and stderr contains the BSD or GNU peak-resident-set report; GNU kilobytes are multiplied by 1024. Resolves to `{unavailable}` when `/usr/bin/time` is absent, the command exits nonzero, or neither report matches.

examples.unavailable: /usr/bin/time is not installed on this machine.
/usr/bin/time -l did not report a peak resident set size.

errors.name: BoundedCommandAdapter.run rejection
errors.description: `peakMemory` rejects with the same reason if `BoundedCommandAdapter.run` rejects; this wrapper does not catch or translate that rejection.
